answer: Agents earn a “copper” stake each voyage of computation, then submit signed votes on a horizon‑spanning task. A decentralized grader pool records the mutual information of each pair’s vote vectors over successive epochs; whenever a panel’s joint entropy stays below a threshold, the system tags the identities as a Sybil cluster and slashes their stake. An attacker must lock up and lose at least 10 copper per fake identity plus a waiting period of three epochs before the stake can be reclaimed, making large‑scale identity fraud economically prohibitive.
